notes.subtopic: 1. Big Picture — Mutiny or War of Independence?

fiveW.who: Indian sepoys, rulers, zamindars and people vs the East India Company
fiveW.where: Meerut → Delhi, Lucknow, Kanpur, Jhansi, Gwalior, Arrah
fiveW.what: The biggest uprising against British rule
fiveW.why: A century of unfair, oppressive and exploitative British rule; greased cartridges
fiveW.how: Sepoys rebelled, marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar their leader

notes.content:
**Executive summary:** Plassey (1757) began British political control; over the next **100 years** the British used unfair, oppressive methods → resentment → **Uprising of 1857**.
• British historians: **'Sepoy Mutiny'**.
• Indians: **'First War of Independence'** — it failed, but sowed the seeds of **nationalism**.

**Chapter map:** Causes (political, economic, socio-religious, military, immediate) → Spread (Meerut, Delhi, Awadh, Kanpur, Arrah, Jhansi, Gwalior) → Why it failed → Effects (Queen's Proclamation).

**Political causes**
• **Doctrine of Lapse** (Dalhousie) — unjust annexations (Jhansi, Nagpur, Satara).
• Bahadur Shah's successors denied **Mughal property and imperial titles**.
• **Annexation of Awadh (1856)** despite loyalty to the Subsidiary Alliance → rulers felt insecure.
• British were quick to **break treaties** → mistrust.

**Economic causes**
• **Heavy land revenue** (Permanent, Ryotwari Settlements) → peasant misery.
• Peasants forced to grow **indigo** and other cash crops for Britain.
• Cheap raw materials bought, cheap British goods sold → Indian economy damaged.
• **Artisans ruined** by duty-free British goods.
• Annexations **confiscated zamindari rights** → zamindars led rebels.

fiveW.who: Hindu and Muslim sepoys of the Bengal Army
fiveW.why: Rumour that the grease contained cow and pig fat
fiveW.how: Sepoys refused the cartridges, were punished and imprisoned, and rebelled

notes.content:
**Socio-religious causes**
• Indians treated as **inferior**; excluded from high posts.
• Activities of **Christian missionaries** alarmed people.
• Reforms like **abolition of sati** and **widow remarriage** seen as interference in customs.
• **Western education** favoured over traditional learning.

**Military causes**
• **Harsh treatment** of sepoys by British officers.
• **General Service Enlistment Act (1856)** — recruits had to serve **overseas**; crossing the sea was believed to cause **loss of caste**.
• Sepoys paid **much less** than British soldiers.

**Immediate cause — Enfield rifle**
• **Greased cartridges** had to be **bitten off**.
• Rumour: grease contained **cow and pig fat** → offended **both Hindus and Muslims**.
• Sepoys who refused were **severely punished and imprisoned** → anger.

fiveW.who: Sepoys of Meerut; Bahadur Shah Zafar
fiveW.what: Outbreak of the revolt; Mughal emperor proclaimed leader
fiveW.how: Attacked the jail, freed prisoners, marched to Delhi

notes.content:
• Sepoys at **Meerut** attacked the jail, **freed their comrades** and **marched to Delhi**.
• Joined by local sepoys; revolt spread through Delhi.
• Rebels proclaimed **Bahadur Shah Zafar** leader — a symbolic **revival of the Mughal Empire**.
• British reinforcements from **Punjab** recaptured Delhi; hundreds killed, many **hanged without trial**.
• **Bahadur Shah** taken prisoner, tried and **exiled to Rangoon** (Burma).

**Primary source:** a British officer's letter boasts that Delhi residents hiding in houses were **bayoneted** — showing the **brutality** of the British revenge.

**Topper extra:** earlier, on **29 March 1857**, sepoy **Mangal Pandey** attacked officers at **Barrackpore**.

The revolt spread to the **North-Western Provinces, central India and Bihar**; British behaviour increased discontent.

| Centre | Leader | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| **Lucknow (Awadh)** | Rebels (Begum Hazrat Mahal) | Besieged the residence of **Sir Henry Lawrence**, British Commissioner; Lucknow later recovered by the British |
| **Kanpur** | **Nana Sahib** — adopted son of **Baji Rao II** | Besieged the British entrenchment; British recaptured Kanpur; Nana escaped; general **Tantia Tope** fought on |
| **Arrah (Bihar)** | **Kunwar Singh**, aged **80** | Led the revolt in Bihar |
| **Jhansi / Gwalior** | **Rani Lakshmibai** + Tantia Tope | See next note |
| **Delhi** | Bahadur Shah Zafar | Symbolic leader |

fiveW.who: Rani Lakshmibai, with Tantia Tope and Bundelkhand rebels
fiveW.why: Jhansi annexed in 1853 under the Doctrine of Lapse
fiveW.how: Organised troops, escaped the siege of Jhansi, captured Gwalior fort, fought to the end

notes.content:
• **Jhansi** (south-west Uttar Pradesh) annexed in **1853** under the Doctrine of Lapse.
• Lakshmibai organised troops, supported by rebels of **Bundelkhand**.
• **1858** — British counter-offensive; after a fierce battle at Jhansi fort she **refused to surrender and escaped**.
• With **Tantia Tope** she captured **Gwalior** — seized its treasury and arsenal.
• **Killed in combat** fighting the British counter-attack.
• Became a **symbol of bravery** and inspiration for later freedom fighters.

• **No coordination**, no common plan.
• **No central leadership**; leaders sought **personal territorial gains** — the idea of a **nation state** did not exist yet.
• **Outdated weapons** vs modern British arms; **lack of money**.
• **Localised** — **South India unaffected**.
• Many **princes and zamindars stayed loyal** to the British.
• **Peasants** (the majority) remained **indifferent**.
• By the end of 1857 the British regained major centres; peace in **1858**.

fiveW.what: Company rule ended; India under the British Crown
fiveW.why: The revolt showed that Company rule had failed
fiveW.how: Royal Proclamation; Secretary of State and Viceroy created; army reorganised

notes.content:
• **Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858)** — India passed **directly under the British Crown**; Company rule ended.
• New office of **Secretary of State for India**.
• Governor-General became **Viceroy** — first Viceroy **Lord Canning**.
• **Doctrine of Lapse abolished**; **adoption rights** restored; treaties with princes to be honoured.
• Promise of **welfare** and **no interference in social and religious customs**.
• Army **reorganised**; more **British soldiers**.
• **Nationalism** — heroism of leaders inspired Indians; awareness of exploitative rule → seen as the **first step towards independence**.

**Comparative history:** the **Opium Wars** — China was defeated by Britain (and France) over the opium trade.

questions.question: When and where did the revolt start? What was its immediate cause?
questions.answer:
• It started in May 1857 at the Meerut cantonment.
  • Immediate cause: the Enfield rifle's greased cartridges, which had to be bitten off; rumour said the grease was cow and pig fat, offending Hindus and Muslims. Sepoys who refused were punished and imprisoned.

questions.question: Discuss the political causes of the Revolt of 1857.
questions.answer:
• Doctrine of Lapse — Dalhousie annexed Jhansi, Nagpur, Satara.
  • Bahadur Shah's successors were denied Mughal property and titles.
  • Annexation of Awadh (1856) despite its loyalty — made rulers insecure.
  • The British broke treaties easily, so rulers mistrusted them.

questions.question: Explain the economic causes of the Revolt of 1857.
questions.answer:
• Heavy land revenue under the Permanent and Ryotwari Settlements.
  • Peasants forced to grow indigo for British needs.
  • Cheap raw materials taken, cheap British goods sold — economy ruined; artisans lost livelihoods.
  • Annexations confiscated zamindari rights, so zamindars led the rebels.

questions.question: What were the socio-religious causes of the Revolt?
questions.answer:
• Indians treated as inferior and kept out of high posts.
  • Growing activities of Christian missionaries.
  • Reforms like abolition of sati and widow remarriage seen as interference.
  • Western education preferred over traditional learning.

questions.question: What were the military causes of the Revolt?
questions.answer:
• Harsh treatment of sepoys by British officers.
  • General Service Enlistment Act (1856) — overseas service; sea travel believed to cause loss of caste.
  • Sepoys were paid much less than British soldiers.

questions.question: Describe the role of Rani Lakshmibai in the Revolt of 1857.
questions.answer:
• Jhansi was annexed in 1853 under the Doctrine of Lapse.
  • She organised her troops, supported by Bundelkhand rebels.
  • In 1858, after a fierce battle at Jhansi fort, she refused to surrender and escaped.
  • With Tantia Tope she captured Gwalior (treasury and arsenal); she was killed in battle — a lasting symbol of courage.

questions.question: Why did the Revolt of 1857 fail? Which regions and groups did not support it?
questions.answer:
• No coordination or common plan; no central leadership; leaders sought personal gains.
  • Outdated weapons and lack of money.
  • Localised — South India was unaffected.
  • Many princes and zamindars stayed loyal to the British; peasants remained indifferent.
questions.topperTip: Mention 'no idea of a nation state yet' — shows deeper understanding.

questions.question: What were the effects of the Revolt of 1857?
questions.answer:
• Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858) — India under the British Crown; Company rule ended.
  • Secretary of State for India created; Governor-General became Viceroy (first: Lord Canning).
  • Doctrine of Lapse abolished; adoption allowed; treaties honoured.
  • Promise of welfare and no interference in religion.
  • Army reorganised with more British soldiers.
  • Birth of nationalism — the first step towards independence.

questions.question: (Picture) Empress of India: name her, when she issued the Proclamation and which policy it abolished.
(Source) A British officer writes that Delhi residents hiding in houses were bayoneted. Which event is this? What is his attitude?
questions.answer:
• The British recapture of Delhi (1857) after the revolt.
  • His attitude is cruel, vengeful and contemptuous — he is 'glad' that even innocent residents, not mutineers, were killed; it exposes the myth of 'mild' British rule.

questions.question: Was the Revolt of 1857 merely a sepoy mutiny or the First War of Independence? Justify.
questions.answer:
• Mutiny view: it began among sepoys over cartridges; it was localised and lacked a national plan.
  • War of Independence view: rulers, zamindars, artisans and peasants in many regions joined; Hindus and Muslims fought together under Bahadur Shah; its causes were political, economic and social, not only military.
  • Conclusion: more than a mutiny — it created national awareness and inspired future freedom fighters.
questions.topperTip: Present both views, then give your conclusion — the classic topper structure.
